previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: James, a man with a history of alcohol abuse, COPD, and recurrent pneumonia, was admitted after being found down following heavy alcohol intake. He presented with hypoxia, shortness of breath, and cough productive of green sputum. He was treated for pneumonia with Bactrim, guided by sputum culture showing Staph aureus sensitive to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, and for alcohol withdrawal with high-dose diazepam. His oxygen levels improved, and he was weaned to room air. Despite refusing nebulizer treatments, his respiratory status stabilized. Due to his pattern of repeated admissions and incomplete treatment courses, a Section 35 was initiated, and he was discharged in police custody for admission to an alcohol treatment facility. He was medically stable at discharge, with plans to complete his antibiotic course and continue vitamin supplementation and blood pressure medications.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo M with h/o HTN, COPD, alcohol abuse, and recent PNAs

# Shortness of breath: The nightfloat resident was unable to get

was consulted upon arrival but patient was intoxicated so no 
assessment was made on their end, though she did confirm that Mr 
___ was discharged from ___ prior to the official end

was started on treatment for COPD exac in the ED. CXR not 
suggestive on pna and no leukocytosis now so suspicion for 
infection was low.  He was given steroids in the ED and started 
on Azithromycin and oral prednisone when he hit the floor.  
Patient was not acutely hypoxic but put on 2L NC for symptomatic 
relief and albuterol ipratropium nebs were administered and he 
was continued on his fluticasone/salmeterol diskus.  ACS was r/o 
with normal ECG and negative tropes.  Patient was assessed for 
an ambulatory saturation to which he was 96% on room air.  The 
next day the patient stated his breathing felt much better and 
he wanted to be discharged.

in the setting of EtOH intoxication. EtOH level at 300.  Patient 
was put on CIWA precautions with Diazepam 5 mg q 6 hrs prn, 
banana bag, thiamine, folate, MVI.  He was somewhat restless 
throughout the day and a half during this admission and had 3 
CIWA scores over 10 for which he received diazepam.  He was also 
somewhat tremulous the morning of discharge but patient was very 
eager for discharge.  He states his friend called him and that 
he got his job back from 1 month prior and also that he had 
plans to stay with his friend.

continued his home enalapril 10 mg daily, HCTZ 25 mg daily, and
